messages:
ravi: quick thread: proposal for a compact tensor-index sidecar to speed safetensors partial loads + provide signed offsets for safe range reads. want quick sanity checks.

anya: sounds useful. sketch the invariants you want it to satisfy.

ravi: minimal: 1) immutable mapping from tensor->byte range, 2) signed by ingest to prove authenticity, 3) supports per-tensor checksum optional, 4) read_window guidance for aligned reads, 5) shard-id for sharded checkpoints.

claire: re: 4, read_window is critical. runtime should be able to request an aligned range that covers the tensor but is page-aligned to avoid extra mmap overhead. include preferred_alignment and padded_start/padded_end.

ravi: yep. schema idea: newline-delimited JSON objects: {"tensor":"layer_0.weight","shard":"s0","offset":12345,"length":54321,"dtype":"f32","shape":"[4096,4096]","sha256":"...","read_window":{"start":12288,"end":57344}}

anya: where do we store the sidecar? same bucket, key: <checkpoint>.index.jsonl or <checkpoint>.index.bin for compact form. signed metadata stored in catalog with signature blob.

claire: signing flow: ingest-worker computes index, writes sidecar, calls KMS to sign digest(index) -> writes signature to checkpoint metadata. runtime validates signature before trusting ranges.

ravi: optional binary index: flatbuffer or protobuf to cut bytes and parsing time. but keep JSONl as visible fallback.

anya: how do we compute per-tensor offsets for safetensors without full parse cost? staging-worker must parse header once during ingest; that's expected. for big files we already do a staging pass to compute checksums so piggyback index generation there.

claire: make per-tensor checksum optional. policy: compute them for tensors > 64MB or when require_tensor_checksums flag is set. cheaper workloads skip to file-level checksum.

ravi: sharding: include shard object path and allow index entries to reference same tensor across multiple shards (for interleaved layouts). runtime picks earliest matching shard-id in its region.

anya: operational concerns: indexing increases ingest latency. mitigation: write checkpoint as committed with indexing_pending flag. runtime can still stream whole-file but will prefer committed+indexed for fast warmup. index should be backfilled by background job.

claire: safety: sidecar must be validated against object-size and file-level sha256 before accepting signature. ingest-worker should compute both to avoid mismatches.

ravi: APIs: GET /checkpoint/{id}/index -> returns index manifest (signed metadata + url). GET /checkpoint/{id}/index/{tensor} -> returns read_window + shard info. also support range-presigned urls for immediate fetch of read_window.

anya: metrics to add: index_generation_time, index_size_bytes, index_hit_rate, index_validation_errors. add audit logs linking index signatures to ingest user.

claire: migration: mark existing checkpoints as legacy_no_index. runtime falls back to header-parse path. schedule background indexer to upgrade popular models first.

ingest-bot: note: staging job spike scheduled by anya for next week.

ravi: ok i'll draft a short RFC and include schema + KMS signing flow + migration plan. thanks for the quick checks.

runtime-svc: +1 for read_window API and presigned range urls. this will cut warmup latency for short prompt workloads.
